Diagnosis:
The failing test `testEscapedQuote_LANG_477` uses the pattern `"it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!"` with an ExtendedMessageFormat instantiated with a custom format registry. The bug report indicates an OutOfMemoryError when using ExtendedMessageFormat with a custom format registry and a pattern containing single quotes.

Looking at the relevant code, the ExtendedMessageFormat constructor with the pattern, locale, and registry assigns the registry and calls applyPattern. In applyPattern, the pattern is parsed character by character. When a quote character (`'`) is found, appendQuotedString is called. The logic inside appendQuotedString tries to handle escaped quotes (two single quotes `''`) by appending one quote to the output and moving the position forward.

The parsing method applyPattern also detects format elements, parses formats using parseFormatDescription, and attempts to get a Format instance from the custom registry using getFormat.

The problem likely arises in the handling of the single quotes in the pattern in conjunction with the custom registry. The custom registry triggers getFormat to try to get a format instance, possibly creating some recursive or unbounded behavior (as indicated by the OutOfMemoryError in the bug report). The specific pattern `"it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!"` contains both escaped quotes (`''` -> `'`) and quoted literals (`'test'`), so the parsing code must correctly handle these quote sequences.

In appendQuotedString, the code detects escaped quotes with the `ESCAPED_QUOTE` substring (which is `''`), appends a single quote, and moves forward. However, the code looks like it could be mishandling quotes by incorrectly appending or not advancing position correctly, especially if escaping is enabled and quotes are nested or adjacent. This mishandling might lead to an infinite loop or unbounded recursive call in applyPattern.

Thus, the root cause is likely that the quote parsing in appendQuotedString, specifically handling of escaped quotes and quoted literals inside patterns with a custom registry, is incorrect. This results in applyPattern not advancing or processing the input correctly, causing excessive memory use and thus an OutOfMemoryError.

The likely root cause is the incorrect or incomplete handling of escaped single quotes and quoted strings by appendQuotedString or the interaction of this with applyPattern and registry-based format resolution.

Recent issue reports are unrelated, so no further insight there.

In summary, the mishandling of single quotes in conjunction with the custom format registry in ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern and appendQuotedString causes an infinite loop or excessive memory use leading to OutOfMemoryError.

Next, I will suggest which methods should be fixed.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(java.lang.String, java.text.ParsePosition, java.lang.StringBuffer, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
